learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge at a constructive level of the main components of power plants equipped with steam and/or gas turbines
Design real power cycles used in the field of thermal engines and refrigeration systems.
Ability for the design and optimization of vapor and gas compression refrigeration cycles and cryogenic cycles.
Ability for the design and optimization of power cycles with steam turbines, gas turbines, and combined cycles.
Ability to calculate energy, mass, and volumetric balances in combustion systems
Know constructive elements of power and refrigeration plants
General knowledge of thermal engines and their classification
Design heat production systems from fuels.
Ability to design and optimize cogeneration systems.

syllabus_topics: Power cycles of plants equipped with steam turbines. Introduction.
Common modifications of the Rankine cycle.
Power cycles of plants equipped with gas turbines. Introduction.
The thermodynamic cycle of gas turbines.
Constructive elements of power plants. Constructive elements of steam cycles.
Power plants based on combined cycles Introduction
The heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) of TV-TG combined cycles
Refrigeration cycles Introduction. The inverse Carnot cycle.
Complete or incomplete, rich or lean combustion.
Combustion efficiency or heat utilization factor
teaching_methods: Use of software (e.g. Cycle Pad, EES)
assessment_rules: The passing grade is 5 points out of 10. Students can choose between a progressive evaluation system or a global exam. For progressive evaluation, students must complete two block exams (27.5% each) and a long problem exam (45%), requiring a minimum of 3.5 points in theory average and 3.5 in the long problem, plus an overall score of 5 or higher. The global and extraordinary evaluations consist of a single written exam covering all course content, weighted at 100%, and require a minimum score of 5 points. Mandatory attendance of at least 80% of laboratory practices is required; failure to meet this limits the maximum possible grade to 4.0. Active participation in practices can add a 10% bonus to the final grade if it exceeds 5.0, or 5% if it is below 5.0. Copying or using electronic devices during exams results in a 0 for that test.
